clue.text: Page having to load up and ride a cycle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for load is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to lade is to load a ship or cart

explanation.surface: A pageboy is told to load up the delivery bike and pedal off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the reversal signal, fitting for a down clue; 'ride a cycle' is the verb sense, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to push the cranks of a bicycle, which is how you ride it.

clue.text: Start giving directions to a solicitor

parts.note: S for south and E for east are two compass directions
E for east is the second compass direction
a tout solicits custom, pestering people to buy

explanation.surface: A newcomer begins by asking a lawyer the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits business: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out on a journey is to begin it.

clue.text: Laboured, so will be taxed

explanation.surface: Someone complains that hard work will only lead to more tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so will be' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboured prose seems forced and effortful; something taxed is put under heavy pressure or stress.

clue.text: Learning one must include the French siren

indicators.note: the word for learning plus one must hold something inside, between its letters

parts.note: lore is a body of learning or traditional knowledge
I is the Roman numeral for one
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A student is told that learning must take in a French temptress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must include' tells you the French article sits inside learning plus one. The Lorelei is the rock-maiden of the Rhine in German legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the Lorelei lured Rhine boatmen to their deaths with song, exactly as a siren did.

clue.text: He's produced notedly original work

parts.note: notedly is a pun: the work is made of musical notes rather than being famously original

explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes music produces original works made of notes.

clue.text: Cheats on the hard worker in agreement

parts.note: cons are swindles or cheats
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A diligent employee is cheated, and somehow everyone goes along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonant can mean harmonious or in accord with something, as in consonant with the facts.

clue.text: Enter into arrangement for maintenance

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters means the words enter and into are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone signs up for a maintenance deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' signals that ENTER and INTO are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the keeping or preserving of something, like keeping it maintained.

clue.text: Favour incorporating the right element

indicators.note: incorporating means the word for favour takes a letter into its body

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing

explanation.surface: A grant or favour that brings in the correct ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Boron is a chemical element, atomic number five.

clue.text: Untie reef knots

indicators.note: tying the word reef in knots means its letters get tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to undo the reef knots.
explanation.walkthrough: Reef knots are real sailing knots, so the surface reads naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something is to release or untie it.

clue.text: Some of the aristocracy stop on time

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Some aristocrats are told to halt on time.
explanation.definitionFit: The baronage is the body of barons, one rank of the nobility.

clue.text: The rest may have to sit again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: The remaining models may have to sit for the painter once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may have to' is a link word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is rest or relaxation.

clue.text: Heads back to deliver a knock-out blow

indicators.note: back means the slang word for heads is read in the other direction

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A boxer aims for the head to knock an opponent out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to knock someone senseless with a blow.

clue.text: Service flat — bargain price!

parts.note: even means level or flat
to buy something for a song is to get it very cheaply

explanation.surface: An advert for an apartment at a knock-down price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home, but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening church service.

clue.text: Bring back control over the land

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first word sits above the second

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse
a state is a nation or land

explanation.surface: A ruler resolves to restore control over the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former position.

clue.text: By the shore setting seed is a problem

indicators.note: problem signals that the words seed is a must be worked out into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener finds coastal ground a struggle for sowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside resort is a place by the sea, on the coast.

clue.text: Make a song about heat in crowds

indicators.note: about means the singing word goes around another

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
to warm is to heat

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about the heat in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a song about' sounds like the idiom for making a fuss, but it splits: the singing word goes 'about' (around) the word for heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming means moving in a dense, teeming mass.

clue.text: In this way a combine is rising to great heights

parts.note: so can mean thus, in this way
a ring is a group or cartel acting together, a combine

explanation.surface: A combine harvester seems to lift off into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' suggests farm machinery, but means a cartel, a RING. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaring flies or climbs high into the air.

clue.text: Getting on top of the players is not very bright!

parts.note: over means above, on top of
the cast are the actors in a play

explanation.surface: A critic says an actor who upstages the rest is not very clever.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is clouded over and dull, so not bright.

clue.text: Marked in dates for settlement

indicators.note: settlement suggests the letters of in dates being settled into a new order

explanation.surface: Dates are noted down for settling a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stained is marked or discoloured.

clue.text: Such medication can really get up one's nose!

definitions.text: Such medication can really get up one's nose!

parts.words: Such medication can really get up one's nose!
parts.note: get up one's nose is an idiom for irritate, but here it is literal: the medicine is breathed in through the nostrils

explanation.definitionFit: Medicine that is breathed in through the nose or mouth goes up into the airways.

clue.text: Derived from local sources as well

indicators.note: derived from means the letters come from within the words local sources

explanation.surface: A claim that information also came from local sources.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means too, in addition.

clue.text: A nymph's sound reflection

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth a mountain nymph who pined until only her voice remained
a sound bounced back from a surface

explanation.surface: A nymph's voice bounces off the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain nymph of Greek myth wasted away to a voice; the word also means a repeated sound returning from a wall.

clue.text: Kind fellow put in the shade

indicators.note: put in means the word for fellow goes inside the word for shade

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A friendly chap is moved out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests shadow, but is a colour, HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate and kind.

clue.text: A monk sick of fish

parts.note: Br is the abbreviation for Brother, the title of a monk
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A monk is made ill by fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' and 'of' are link words. BRILL is a flatfish like turbot.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: Good man, a chemist, creates an impression

parts.note: St for saint, a good man
MPS, Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a British pharmacist's qualification

explanation.surface: A kindly pharmacist makes a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: MPS stands for Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a qualification of British dispensing chemists.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp something is to press a mark or imprint into it.

clue.text: The new American private

indicators.note: new means the word American is made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A new American soldier, a private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is a link word. 'private' suggests a soldier, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing held in camera is held in private, away from the public.

clue.text: It's hard to get on in a beastly place

indicators.note: in means the word on goes inside the word for a pigpen

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs, a place for beasts

explanation.surface: Getting ahead in a beastly place is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony means rock-like, so hard.

clue.text: Drink alone. — that's not to be taken seriously!

parts.note: tea is a drink
singly means one at a time, alone

explanation.surface: Someone sipping tea alone insists it is not serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said teasingly is said in jest, mockingly.
